newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-FORMER HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION TAKES SPLIT DECISION.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-FORMER HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION TAKES SPLIT DECISION.

text.p: Former heavyweight champion Larry Holmes eked out a split-decision victory over unheralded Maurice Harris on Tuesday in his first fight at Madison Square Garden in 18 years.

The 47-year-old Holmes, who returned to the Garden for the first time since defending his title in 1979, took an early lead and then hung on for a tight, disputed victory over an opponent 25 years his junior.
Holmes dominated the action from a distance but Harris was able to score inside and easily late in the fight.

Judge Harold Lederman had the bout 96-94 in favour of Holmes and George Colon saw it 96-95 for the former champion, but Joe Dwyer scored its 96-94 for Harris. Colon scored the last round 10-10 and cost Harris, who appeared to have clearly won the round, a draw.

"My performance was okay," said Holmes. "He really didn't want to fight. If I was a man of 22 years old fighting a 47-year-old I would have put him away. It goes down as a win and I did what I had to do to get a decision."
"He knew he lost," Harris said. "He didn't hit me with anything. He hit me with his best and I didn't go anywhere."
Holmes (66-6) held the heavyweight championship for more than seven years, capturing the title in 1978 when he scored a 15-round decision over Ken Norton.

During his seven-year reign, he defended the heavyweight crown 20 times before losing to Michael Spinks in his 49th fight, which fell one short Rocky Marciano's record for consecutive wins by a heavyweight.
In his last two fights, Holmes has now won a tight split decision and lost a close, disputed split decision.
